Fit the propensity model set with cross-fitting

Source: R/fit_propensity_models.R
fit_propensity_models.Rd

Fits every model of a propensity model set, the tree algorithms once per seed. The default is the set evaluated in a manuscript in preparation, the same as in propensity_sensitivity(): logistic regression with main effects, BART and the GRF probability forest (three seeds each), with the same settings. The faster set of logistic regression, random forests and gradient boosting is available with algorithms = c("logistic_regression", "random_forest", "gradient_boosting"). Scores are cross-fitted by default: the fold assignment is stratified by treatment, derived from seed, and shared by every model; for each fold the model is fitted on the other folds and predicts the held-out fold. Probabilities are clipped to [clip, 1 - clip], turned into logits, and ranked (percentile rank = rank(logit, ties = "average") / n).

Usage

fit_propensity_models(
  formula,
  data,
  algorithms = c("logistic_regression", "bart", "grf_probability"),
  seeds = 1:3,
  folds = 5,
  cross_fit = TRUE,
  n_trees = NULL,
  quality_tolerance = 0.05,
  clip = 0.001,
  cores = 1,
  seed = 1
)

# S3 method for class 'propensity_model_set'
print(x, digits = 4, ...)

Arguments

formula

A two-sided formula such as treat ~ x1 + x2. The left-hand side is the treatment and must be numeric, coded 0/1. Factor covariates are expanded to dummies for the tree algorithms.

data

A data frame holding every variable in formula. Missing values are an error: impute first.

algorithms

Which algorithms to fit. The default, c("logistic_regression", "bart", "grf_probability"), is the set evaluated in a manuscript in preparation and the default of propensity_sensitivity(): "bart" (dbarts::bart2, default priors, 75 trees, 500 burn-in and 500 kept draws in each of 4 chains, one thread; the score is the posterior-mean probability) and "grf_probability" (grf::probability_forest, honest splitting, 2,000 trees, one thread; out-of-bag predictions when cross_fit = FALSE), both on the dummy-coded design matrix. The faster set, "random_forest" and "gradient_boosting" with logistic regression, is not part of that evaluation. Also exploratory, logistic regression variants on the same design matrix: "logistic_splines" (fitted once; natural cubic splines, splines::ns(df = 3), on every column with at least 5 distinct values in the training rows whose two interior knots are distinct and inside its range, the other columns linear), "lasso" (glmnet::cv.glmnet, binomial, lambda.min from 5 internal folds that differ by seed) and "lasso_interactions" (the same on the main effects plus all two-way products of the design columns); the lasso variants need the package 'glmnet'.

seeds

Integer vector; one tree model per seed. Logistic regression is fitted once.

folds

Number of cross-fitting folds (at least 2).

cross_fit

TRUE for out-of-fold scores (default); FALSE for the "as MatchIt does it" mode described above.

n_trees

NULL to choose the gradient boosting tree count once by cross-validation, or a positive integer to use as is.

quality_tolerance

Relative log-loss tolerance of the quality gate (default 0.05).

clip

Probabilities are clipped to [clip, 1 - clip] before the logit.

cores

Number of cores for the model tasks (default 1).

seed

Integer seed from which every other seed is derived.

x

A propensity_model_set object.

digits

Digits for the quality numbers.

...

Not used.

Value

An object of class "propensity_model_set": a list with logit, rank and probability (n x M matrices whose column names are the model ids, for example "logistic_regression_1", "random_forest_2"), models (data frame with model_id, algorithm, seed_index, task_seed, n_trees, logloss, brier, c_statistic, passed_logloss_gate), folds (integer fold assignment), treatment, formula, logistic_log (cross-fitting only: one row per logistic model and fold with the prediction path ("formula", "design_unseen_levels" or "design_fallback_predict_error"), glm_not_converged and glm_fitted_0_or_1; NULL without logistic regression), settings (every argument plus the fixed tree settings and the chosen tree count) and call.

Fixed settings

Random forest: ntree = 500, mtry = floor(sqrt(p)), nodesize = 10. Gradient boosting: distribution = "bernoulli", interaction.depth = 3, shrinkage = 0.05, bag.fraction = 0.8; the number of trees is frozen: when n_trees is NULL it is chosen once by 5-fold cross-validation on the full data (gbm with cv.folds = 5, capped at 3,000 trees, derived seed) and then used unchanged for every seed and every fold; when n_trees is given it is used as is.

Seeds and parallel runs

Per-task seeds are derived in the main process from seed and the model index, passed to each worker and applied with withr::with_seed(), which restores the random number generator state afterwards. Results are identical for cores = 1 and cores > 1. Parallel runs use parallel::mclapply() on Unix and fall back to a serial run on Windows.

The "as MatchIt does it" mode

With cross_fit = FALSE the scores are in-sample predictions for logistic regression and gradient boosting and out-of-bag predictions for the random forest. This mirrors what MatchIt::matchit() returns for distance = "glm", "gbm" and "randomforest", so that applied users can compare with their own object. In-sample tree scores are overfit and shrink overlap, which is why cross-fitting is the default.

Quality gate

The models table reports the cross-fitted log-loss, Brier score and c-statistic (rank-based AUC). passed_logloss_gate is TRUE when the log-loss is at most (1 + quality_tolerance) times the best model's log-loss. The balance part of the quality gate (post-match maximum absolute standardized mean difference on main terms at most 0.10) needs the matches and is applied later by the wrapper propensity_sensitivity(), not here.

Examples

data("lalonde", package = "MatchIt")
model_set <- fit_propensity_models(
  treat ~ age + educ + race + married + nodegree + re74 + re75,
  data = lalonde, seeds = 1, n_trees = 100,
  algorithms = c("logistic_regression", "random_forest", "gradient_boosting")
)
model_set
#> Propensity model set: 3 model(s), 614 patients, 185 treated
#> Scores: 5-fold cross-fitted scores; probabilities clipped to [0.001, 0.999]
#> Gradient boosting trees: 100 (supplied)
#> Log-loss gate: within 5 % of the best model (balance part applied after matching)
#>               model_id logloss  brier c_statistic passed_logloss_gate
#>  logistic_regression_1  0.4123 0.1338      0.8612               FALSE
#>        random_forest_1  0.3634 0.1143      0.9014                TRUE
#>    gradient_boosting_1  0.3513 0.1110      0.9091                TRUE
head(model_set$rank)

# Default: logistic regression, BART x 3 and GRF x 3 (slower).
full_set <- fit_propensity_models(
  treat ~ age + educ + race + married + nodegree + re74 + re75,

)
